sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Douglas County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the load. The Appraisal Department places values and takes appeals for the Board of Assessors. The elected Tax Commissioner mails bills, collects payment and accepts homestead applications, and that office's website explains the bill, assessment notices, exemptions, delinquent taxes and tax sales.

  • Appraisal Department: write to 8700 Hospital Dr., Douglasville, GA 30134 or call 770-920-7228. Walk-in filing is on the annex's second floor at 6200 Fairburn Rd.
  • Tax Commissioner: ground-level office in the Government Annex, serving the public weekdays except for a lunch closure at noon, with the last line cut off early to allow it.
  • Finance Department: publishes millage rate documents and hearing dates, and its 2026 packet carries a September 4 revision.

Field appraisers also canvass neighborhoods. Citing O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1, the county says they check permit status and review new construction, additions, remodels, sales and appeals, measuring and photographing as they go. Each wears a photo badge and drives a marked vehicle.

sections.h2: When were Douglas County's 2026 assessment notices mailed and when did appeals close?
sections.html:
Annual notices for 2026 went into the mail on June 16, 2026, and appeals were due by 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026, a date now in the past. The department warns in capital letters that it cannot move the deadline, and it urges owners to file early and keep a copy for themselves.

In a normal cycle notices are mailed sometime from April 15 to July 1, and the 45 days count from the date on the notice. A filing can go by post, over the counter or through the online property search, and a dropbox in the annex parking lot serves after-hours visits. Fax and email filings are refused. A representative must attach a letter of authorization.

Ask the department for your property record card and the comparable sales on file before deciding to appeal. Personal property owners are notified only when the value changes or the county disagrees with a return filed during the January 1 to April 1 window.

sections.h2: How does a Douglas County appeal move from the assessors to court?
sections.html:
The case climbs through stages, and you can stop at any stage where the number is acceptable. The ordinary route passes through a Board of Equalization whose members the grand jury appoints.

  1. The assessors take a fresh look and mail a written answer, called the 30-day letter, that states whether the value changed.
  2. An unchanged value sends the file directly to the Board of Equalization. A reduced value you accept needs no action, and the appeal lapses after the 30 days.
  3. A changed value you still dispute must be contested in writing to the department within those 30 days.
  4. The Board of Equalization mails notice of a hearing date, and the county recommends appearing with your own proof of market value.
  5. Owner or assessors may carry the ruling to Superior Court within 30 days after it is mailed, paying $25 to the court clerk.

You may pick another route when you file. Arbitration is limited to value. A hearing officer is reserved for non-homestead parcels worth more than $500,000 and hears value and uniformity only. Going straight to Superior Court requires the assessors' consent but allows any argument. State guidance lists the grounds as taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions can Douglas County owners claim?
sections.html:
Applications go to the Tax Commissioner, online or at the counter, and the county takes them all year even though April 1 is the cutoff for the current cycle. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1, and proof means a state ID or driver's license and a vehicle registration at that address. State guidance also lets an owner file during the 45-day appeal window.

Categories on the county's exemption page:

  • The standard homestead exemption.
  • Age 62 and age 65 senior exemptions, plus a 65 fixed-income version with an income requirement.
  • Disability, supported by two kinds of proof or certificates from two doctors, with a Social Security Administration letter.
  • Disabled veteran, shown by a VA statement of service-connected benefits paid at 100 percent on January 1.
  • Surviving spouse of a service member killed in action, or of a police officer or firefighter who died in the line of duty.

State records also place Douglas County on the list of counties with a base-year valuation freeze, which holds taxable value at an earlier year while the owner stays in the home. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the base year and the qualifying rules.

sections.h2: What do Douglas County's housing numbers show?
sections.html:
Douglas County packs about 720 people into each of its 200 square miles of land. The mid-2025 population estimate of 154,293 is 6.9 percent above the 2020 base, and 801 building permits were counted for 2025. The average commute is 33.2 minutes.

Because about two of every three occupied homes have an owner living in them, an assessment jump reaches many households together. Set the value on your notice beside these middle figures and beside nearby sales before choosing to appeal.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when you sell a house in Douglas County?
sections.html:
Georgia puts the year's tax on the January 1 owner and returns nothing to a seller who leaves later. According to state guidance a bill generally allows 60 days for payment, and December 20 is the common due date. Get the exact bill date and balance for your parcel from the Douglas County Tax Commissioner.

The commissioner's website carries delinquent taxes, upcoming tax sales and an excess funds list, so look there for unpaid earlier years. State guidance says county tax liens are filed on the general execution docket in the clerk's office, and the commissioner can say whether one sits on your parcel.

A lot split before sale begins with a survey that goes to the Zoning Administrator for approval. Once the stamped survey is recorded, new deeds are signed and recorded with the clerk, and the Appraisal Department keeps a deed specialist for the tax-side changes. Heirs and owners who are behind on taxes sometimes choose an as-is cash sale so the tax clears at closing and no repairs are needed.

faqs.q: Is the Douglas County 2026 appeal deadline over?
faqs.a: Yes. Notices went out June 16, 2026 and the cutoff was 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026, with no extensions allowed. The next notices will open a new 45-day period.

faqs.q: Will Douglas County take an appeal by fax or email?
faqs.a: No. Use the mail, the annex counter or the online property search. A representative filing for an owner must include a letter of authorization.

faqs.q: What does it cost to take a Douglas County appeal to Superior Court?
faqs.a: The filing fee is $25, paid to the Clerk of Superior Court, and the owner must notify the assessors in writing. Either side may appeal a Board of Equalization decision within 30 days of its mailing.

faqs.q: Which office takes a Douglas County homestead application?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner, online or in person, with a state ID or driver's license and a vehicle registration at the home address. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and April 1 is the usual filing cutoff.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if I sell my Douglas County house in the spring?
faqs.a: The owner of record on January 1 owes for the whole year, and Georgia gives no partial-year refund. The sale contract and settlement statement decide the split, so get a balance from the Tax Commissioner first.
